# Hugh Carrow

## Overview

- **Age:** Almost fourteen at the start of volume 1  <sub>[v1 c15 P24](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0024)</sub>
- **Gender:** Male  <sub>[v1 c15 P28](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0028)</sub>
- **Origin:** Brierley  <sub>[v1 c15 P15](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0015), [v1 c15 P16](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0016), [v1 c38 P49](../source/v01-c38.md#nw-v01-c38-p0049)</sub>
- **Role:** Teacher and college student  <sub>[v1 c36 P24](../source/v01-c36.md#nw-v01-c36-p0024), [v2 c1 P55](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0055), [v3 c5 P0](../source/v03-c05.md#nw-v03-c05-p0000)</sub>
- **Titles:** President of the Brierley Village Improvement Society  <sub>[v2 c6 P8](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0008)</sub>; President of the Freshman Class  <sub>[v3 c5 P0](../source/v03-c05.md#nw-v03-c05-p0000)</sub>; Medalist  <sub>[v1 c36 P3](../source/v01-c36.md#nw-v01-c36-p0003)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** Hughie  <sub>[v1 c15 P24](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0024), [v1 c25 P55](../source/v01-c25.md#nw-v01-c25-p0055)</sub>

## Appearance

Hugh is a tall youth with broad shoulders, wavy chestnut hair, mischievous light-brown or hazel eyes, and a mouth often contorted into a mocking grin. He resembles his father when he was a young man and is considered exceptionally handsome by those around him. After a severe illness, he appears noticeably older, pale, and thin.

_Sources: [v1 c15 P16](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0016), [v1 c15 P28](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0028), [v1 c28 P32](../source/v01-c28.md#nw-v01-c28-p0032), [v1 c37 P37](../source/v01-c37.md#nw-v01-c37-p0037), [v2 c19 P50](../source/v02-c19.md#nw-v02-c19-p0050), [v3 c3 P15](../source/v03-c03.md#nw-v03-c03-p0015), [v3 c39 P22](../source/v03-c39.md#nw-v03-c39-p0022), [v3 c41 P15](../source/v03-c41.md#nw-v03-c41-p0015)_

## Personality

Hugh is lively, cheerful, mischievous, and fond of teasing others, though he is capable of deep remorse when he realizes he has genuinely hurt someone's feelings. He is extremely smart, ambitious, and possesses strong determination, showing high academic drive alongside an appreciation for humor. Popular and manly, he guards his speech and actions to remain worthy of high principles and shows great enthusiasm for leadership and community endeavors.

_Sources: [v1 c15 P16](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0016), [v1 c15 P28](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0028), [v1 c15 P49](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0049), [v1 c30 P24](../source/v01-c30.md#nw-v01-c30-p0024), [v1 c35 P3](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0003), [v2 c1 P55](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0055), [v2 c19 P51](../source/v02-c19.md#nw-v02-c19-p0051), [v3 c5 P0](../source/v03-c05.md#nw-v03-c05-p0000), [v3 c25 P25](../source/v03-c25.md#nw-v03-c25-p0025), [v3 c27 P36](../source/v03-c27.md#nw-v03-c27-p0036)_

## History

After spending three years in Alberta with his father, Hugh returned to Brierley to resume his schooling, quickly establishing himself at the top of his class and competing intensely with Nell Harcourt. His teasing of Nell by calling her 'Carrots' sparked a long-running grudge on her part, despite his immediate remorse and sincere apologies. He later saved Nell from the bridge piling in Gorham Pullen's dory and excelled in the Regent's class, ultimately winning the medalist honors while Nell won the Avery scholarship. To fund his own college education, he taught school in Pale Sands for a year and actively co-founded and led the Brierley Village Improvement Society as its president. He surrendered the Brierley school position to Nell so she could remain near home, which led to a reconciliation and the start of a warm friendship between them. At Wexcombe, Hugh led the Freshmen to victory in the Arts Rush, was elected Freshman Class President, and joined the Lambs fraternity. Although he courted Nell and eventually proposed to her, she declined his romantic advances, prompting him to step back into a distant, polite acquaintance. He pushed himself to academic extremes at university, earning High Honors in Classics and the Cooper Prize, but suffered a life-threatening case of typhoid fever that summer before recovering.
